members.name: expiry_day_pattern_v1
members.thesis: F&O expiry days (weekly Thursday for NIFTY/BANK NIFTY, monthly last Thursday for stocks) exhibit distinct intraday patterns driven by options market makers' gamma hedging and pin risk. On expiry day: (1) stocks/indices tend to pin near the strike with maximum open interest ('max pain'), (2) gamma ex
entry_long: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain < -30 bps) — below max pain, expect pin rally
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close > high_of_last_30_bars AND net_gamma > 0) — gamma squeeze up
entry_short: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain > 30 bps) — above max pain, expect pin pullback
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close < low_of_last_30_bars AND net_gamma < 0) — gamma squeeze down
members.exit_target: morning_pin: price reaches max_pain_strike. afternoon_unwind: 30 bps from entry
members.exit_stop: morning_pin: 15 bps beyond max pain distance (diverging). afternoon_unwind: 15 bps from entry
filters: India_VIX > 12 AND < 25 (need some vol for gamma effects but not too much chaos)
index futures volume > 1.2x normal (confirmed active expiry)
morning: contrarian toward max pain. afternoon: trend-following breakout
weaknesses: Max pain calculation requires full option chain data and is sensitive to OI changes during the day. Stale OI data (even 30-min old) can mislead.
With weekly expiries, every Thursday is an expiry day but gamma effects are smaller for weekly options (less OI). Monthly expiry effects are stronger but only 12 per year.
The afternoon gamma squeeze can be violent and fast — if the stop loss is too tight (15 bps), it may get hit before the squeeze completes.

members.name: expiry_day_premium_decay_v1
members.thesis: On weekly F&O expiry days (Thursdays), Nifty50 and BankNifty constituents experience increased volatility in the first hour due to options hedging/unhedging, followed by a mean reversion toward VWAP as gamma risk decays.
